title: Miso soup with tofu and wakame

source.name: Kokpunkten – Classic dashi, tofu and wakame

ingredients.name: dried wakame
ingredients.prep: soaked in water for 5 minutes, drained
ingredients.original: 2 tbsp dried wakame, soaked in water for 5 minutes, drained

ingredients.name: silken tofu
ingredients.original: 200 g silken tofu, in 1 cm cubes

steps.text: Soak the kombu in the water for 30 minutes if you have time, then heat slowly and remove the kombu just before the water boils.
steps.critical: Take the kombu out before boiling, or the dashi turns slimy and bitter.

steps.text: Bring to a boil, add the bonito flakes, turn off the heat and steep, then strain without squeezing.
Bring the dashi back to a simmer, add the wakame and tofu and heat through.
Turn the heat to low, dissolve the miso in a ladle of dashi and stir it in. Heat without boiling.
steps.critical: Never boil soup after the miso goes in; the aroma disappears.

notes.techniques: Dashi is made by steeping kombu and bonito flakes; miso is added off the boil and dissolved first so it does not clump.
notes.chemistry: Kombu supplies glutamate and bonito supplies inosinate; together they create synergistic umami, much stronger than either alone.
notes.spiceProfile: Savoury, lightly smoky from bonito, salty-sweet from miso, with fresh scallion.
notes.variations: The everyday Japanese miso soup. Vegan versions use a kombu-shiitake dashi, and tonjiru is a hearty pork and root-vegetable version.

title: Vegan miso soup with shiitake dashi

ingredients.name: firm tofu
ingredients.original: 150 g firm tofu, in 1 cm cubes

steps.text: Soak the kombu and shiitake in the water for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat slowly, remove the kombu just before boiling and simmer the shiitake for 5 minutes. Lift out the shiitake, slice them and return to the pot.
Add the onion and simmer until soft, then the tofu and spinach.
Dissolve the miso in a little broth, stir it in off the boil and top with scallion.
steps.critical: Do not boil after adding miso.

notes.techniques: A cold soak extracts flavour from kombu and dried shiitake without any fish.
notes.chemistry: Dried shiitake contribute guanylate, which works with kombu glutamate for strong umami without bonito.
notes.spiceProfile: Earthy and deep, with a saltier, more robust red miso and sweet onion.
notes.variations: Fully plant-based with an earthier taste than bonito dashi. Red miso is stronger and saltier than mixed miso, so less is needed.

title: Tonjiru, pork and root vegetable miso soup

ingredients.name: thinly sliced pork belly
ingredients.original: 200 g thinly sliced pork belly, in 3 cm pieces

ingredients.name: burdock root (gobo)
ingredients.prep: shaved thinly and soaked in water
ingredients.original: 80 g burdock root (gobo), shaved thinly and soaked in water (optional)

ingredients.name: konnyaku
ingredients.original: 150 g konnyaku, torn into small pieces (optional)

steps.text: Fry the pork in the sesame oil until no longer pink.
Add the daikon, carrot, burdock, konnyaku and shiitake and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the dashi, bring to a simmer, skim and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Add the tofu, then dissolve the miso into the soup off the boil.
steps.critical: Add the miso at the end and do not boil it.

steps.text: Serve with scallions and a pinch of shichimi.

notes.techniques: The pork and vegetables are stir-fried before simmering, which adds richness and helps the vegetables keep their shape.
notes.chemistry: Rendered pork fat carries flavour into the broth, and root vegetable starches lightly thicken it.
notes.spiceProfile: Rich and savoury with sweet root vegetables, sesame and optional seven-spice heat.
notes.variations: A hearty meal soup, more like a stew than the light everyday miso soup.
